title: The Federalist Papers
note: The 85 essays written to win ratification; still the most-cited guide to what the framers thought they were building.

title: The Creation of the American Republic, 1776–1787
note: Bancroft Prize-winning account of how American political thought was transformed between independence and the Constitution.

title: The Ideological Origins of the American Revolution
note: Pulitzer and Bancroft Prize winner tracing the pamphlet literature and ideas that drove the Revolution.

title: Original Meanings: Politics and Ideas in the Making of the Constitution
note: Pulitzer Prize-winning history of the Convention and ratification, and a historian's challenge to easy originalism.

title: The Framers' Coup: The Making of the United States Constitution
note: A detailed narrative arguing the Constitution was a conservative reaction against the democratic excesses of the 1780s.

title: Ratification: The People Debate the Constitution, 1787–1788
note: A state-by-state history of the ratification debates and the ordinary Americans who conducted them.

title: Miracle at Philadelphia: The Story of the Constitutional Convention
note: A vivid, highly readable narrative of the summer of 1787.

title: An Economic Interpretation of the Constitution of the United States
note: The provocative classic arguing that the framers' economic interests shaped the Constitution.

title: The Second Founding: How the Civil War and Reconstruction Remade the Constitution
note: A concise history of the Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments and their narrowing by the courts.

title: America's Constitution: A Biography
note: A clause-by-clause tour of the Constitution's text and history, written for general readers.

title: The Bill of Rights: Creation and Reconstruction
note: Argues the Bill of Rights was reshaped by the Fourteenth Amendment, recasting the incorporation debate.

title: Democracy and Distrust: A Theory of Judicial Review
note: The representation-reinforcement theory of judicial review; among the most cited works of American legal scholarship.

title: The Least Dangerous Branch: The Supreme Court at the Bar of Politics
note: Named the 'counter-majoritarian difficulty' and set the agenda for decades of debate about judicial review.

title: We the People, Volume 1: Foundations
note: Introduces 'dualist democracy' and constitutional moments outside the Article V process.

title: We the People, Volume 2: Transformations
note: Applies Ackerman's theory to Reconstruction and the New Deal.

title: Freedom's Law: The Moral Reading of the American Constitution
note: Dworkin's case for reading the Constitution's abstract clauses as moral principles.

title: Taking Rights Seriously
note: The jurisprudential classic on rights as trumps and the role of principle in hard cases.

title: A Matter of Interpretation: Federal Courts and the Law
note: Scalia's short manifesto for textualism and originalism, with responses from Tribe, Dworkin, Glendon and Wood.

title: Reading Law: The Interpretation of Legal Texts
note: A catalogue of 57 canons of construction, the textualist's reference work.

title: The Tempting of America: The Political Seduction of the Law
note: Bork's defense of original understanding, written after his failed Supreme Court nomination.

title: Living Originalism
note: Argues originalism and living constitutionalism are compatible through 'framework originalism'.

title: The Living Constitution
note: A short, clear argument that American constitutional law is a common-law system built on precedent.

title: Restoring the Lost Constitution: The Presumption of Liberty
note: The libertarian originalist case for a presumption of liberty and a narrower federal government.

title: The People Themselves: Popular Constitutionalism and Judicial Review
note: A historical argument that the people, not the courts, were meant to have the final say on the Constitution.

title: Constitutional Fate: Theory of the Constitution
note: Identifies the six 'modalities' of constitutional argument that lawyers actually use.

title: One Case at a Time: Judicial Minimalism on the Supreme Court
note: The case for narrow, shallow decisions that leave hard questions to democratic processes.

title: Taking the Constitution Away from the Courts
note: A provocative argument against judicial supremacy and for a 'populist constitutional law'.

title: Common Good Constitutionalism
note: A classical-legal-tradition challenge to both originalism and progressive living constitutionalism.

title: Constitutional Interpretation: Textual Meaning, Original Intent, and Judicial Review
note: A political scientist's influential defense of originalism grounded in popular sovereignty.

title: Our Undemocratic Constitution: Where the Constitution Goes Wrong (And How We the People Can Correct It)
note: A critique of the Constitution's structural features and a call for a new constitutional convention.

title: America's Unwritten Constitution: The Precedents and Principles We Live By
note: Explores the practices, precedents and principles that supplement the written text.

title: How Rights Went Wrong: Why Our Obsession with Rights Is Tearing America Apart
note: Argues American rights adjudication should borrow proportionality-style balancing from abroad.

title: The Hollow Hope: Can Courts Bring About Social Change?
note: An empirical challenge to the belief that landmark decisions like Brown and Roe produced social change.

title: The Will of the People: How Public Opinion Has Influenced the Supreme Court and Shaped the Meaning of the Constitution
note: A sweeping history showing how the Court has tracked public opinion over two centuries.

title: From Jim Crow to Civil Rights: The Supreme Court and the Struggle for Racial Equality
note: Bancroft Prize winner on the Court's race decisions from Plessy to Brown and the backlash that followed.

title: Simple Justice: The History of Brown v. Board of Education and Black America's Struggle for Equality
note: The definitive narrative history of the litigation campaign that produced Brown.

title: Gideon's Trumpet
note: The story of Clarence Earl Gideon and the right to counsel; a classic introduction to how the Court works.

title: The U.S. Supreme Court: A Very Short Introduction
note: A compact, authoritative primer on the Court's history, procedures and role, by a longtime Court reporter.

title: The Shadow Docket: How the Supreme Court Uses Stealth Rulings to Amass Power and Undermine the Republic
note: How the emergency docket became a major source of the Court's power.

title: The Case Against the Supreme Court
note: A critical history arguing the Court has more often failed than protected minorities.

title: Active Liberty: Interpreting Our Democratic Constitution
note: Justice Breyer's purposive approach to interpretation, framed around democratic participation.

title: A Republic, If You Can Keep It
note: Justice Gorsuch's speeches and opinions on originalism, textualism and the separation of powers.

title: The Unitary Executive: Presidential Power from Washington to Bush
note: A historical defense of presidential control over the executive branch, administration by administration.

title: The Executive Unbound: After the Madisonian Republic
note: Argues that law no longer meaningfully constrains the modern presidency; politics does.

title: The Imperial Presidency
note: The classic warning about the growth of presidential war and secrecy powers.

title: Is Administrative Law Unlawful?
note: A historical attack on agency lawmaking as a revival of extralegal prerogative power.

title: Law and Leviathan: Redeeming the Administrative State
note: A short defense of the administrative state built on the 'morality of administrative law'.

title: War and Responsibility: Constitutional Lessons of Vietnam and Its Aftermath
note: Argues the Constitution requires congressional authorization for war, and that courts should enforce it.

title: Presidential War Power
note: A history of how presidents have taken the war power from Congress.

title: Federalism: Political Identity and Tragic Compromise
note: A skeptical account of the values usually claimed for American federalism.

title: Freedom for the Thought That We Hate: A Biography of the First Amendment
note: A short, lucid history of free speech and press doctrine for general readers.

title: Make No Law: The Sullivan Case and the First Amendment
note: The story of New York Times v. Sullivan and the transformation of libel law.

title: Free Speech and Its Relation to Self-Government
note: The foundational self-governance theory of the First Amendment.

title: A Worthy Tradition: Freedom of Speech in America
note: A masterful, posthumously published survey of free-speech doctrine.

title: Perilous Times: Free Speech in Wartime from the Sedition Act of 1798 to the War on Terrorism
note: Prize-winning history of how civil liberties have fared during national crises.

title: Divided by God: America's Church-State Problem—and What We Should Do About It
note: An accessible history of church-state conflict and a proposal for resolving it.

title: Liberty of Conscience: In Defense of America's Tradition of Religious Equality
note: A philosopher's account of religious liberty grounded in equal respect for conscience.

title: Gunfight: The Battle over the Right to Bear Arms in America
note: A balanced history of gun rights and gun control, built around the Heller litigation.

title: Race, Racism, and American Law
note: The pioneering text that helped launch critical race theory.

title: Abortion: The Clash of Absolutes
note: A constitutional and historical analysis of the abortion debate.

title: Rights Talk: The Impoverishment of Political Discourse
note: A critique of American rights discourse as absolutist and individualistic.

title: The Right to Privacy
note: Case stories illustrating the many strands of the constitutional right to privacy.

title: Takings: Private Property and the Power of Eminent Domain
note: The influential argument for reading the Takings Clause broadly to limit regulation.

title: The Constitution and Criminal Procedure: First Principles
note: Rethinks the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Amendments from first principles.

title: The Collapse of American Criminal Justice
note: Argues constitutional criminal procedure contributed to mass incarceration.

title: Courting Death: The Supreme Court and Capital Punishment
note: A history of the Court's regulation of the death penalty since the 1970s.

title: The Right to Vote: The Contested History of Democracy in the United States
note: The standard history of the expansion and contraction of the franchise.

title: The Supreme Court and Election Law: Judging Equality from Baker v. Carr to Bush v. Gore
note: How the Court entered the 'political thicket' and what equality in voting has come to mean.

title: Constitutional Law: Principles and Policies
note: The standard student treatise, covering every major doctrine clearly and comprehensively.

title: The Constitution of the United States: A Primer for the People
note: A short, plain-English walk through the Constitution's structure and rights.

title: The Penguin Guide to the United States Constitution
note: An annotated text of the Constitution with a concise history and glossary.

title: Federal Jurisdiction
note: The leading student guide to standing, justiciability and the power of the federal courts.
